meta.name: Noumaan
meta.title: Backend Journey
meta.tagline: Finish the Next.js essentials, then follow the Sheryians backend course day by day with the supplementary topics. One page, every date.

phases.name: Next.js essentials only
phases.goal: Finish the topics that matter, at a pace that leaves room for practice. 25 of 48 done is enough to build with.
phases.deliverable: Next.js app deployed on Vercel with env vars
phases.tip: Pace: 1 long video or 2 short ones a day, practice included. Parked for later: CSS Modules, SCSS, i18n, Edge runtime, Middleware, Rewrites, Husky, Lint-Staged.

tasks.title: 27 Recovering from errors, 28 Nested route errors (2 short)
29 Client-side exceptions, 30 Global error handling (2 short)
35 Tailwind v4 in existing projects, 38 Environment variables (2 short)
Deploy to Vercel with env vars, then close the Next.js tab

phases.name: Part A · Days 1–4: Server, npm, MongoDB
phases.goal: Follow the Sheryians video one segment a day.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 4: build a basic Express Notes API with MongoDB CRUD
phases.tip: Do not watch more than the day's timestamp range just to get ahead.

details.label: Topics
items: Course overview and what a server is.
Node.js installation, setup and introduction.

details.label: Supplement to reach 30–50 min (10–20 min)
items: Node.js vs JavaScript in the browser.
What the V8 engine and Node.js runtime do.
Basic client-server request/response flow.

details.label: Practice
items: Install/check Node.js and npm.
Run a JavaScript file with node.
Draw a simple browser → server → response diagram.

tasks.title: Day 2: npm, project setup and REST API introduction · 00:19:45–00:51:02

details.label: Topics
items: APIs and REST API fundamentals.
Creating Notes APIs and testing with Postman.

details.label: Supplement if needed (up to 10–15 min)
items: npm scripts, dependencies and devDependencies.
HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
Request body, route parameters and query parameters.

details.label: Practice
items: Create a small Express project if the video has introduced it.
Test GET and POST requests in Postman.
Explain the difference between an endpoint and an HTTP method.

tasks.title: Day 3: MongoDB connection and database basics · 00:51:02–01:20:00

details.label: Topics
items: MongoDB Atlas setup and database connection.
Mongoose schema/model introduction and saving notes.

details.label: Supplement to reach 30–50 min (5–15 min)
items: SQL vs NoSQL.
Database vs collection vs document.
What Mongoose does and why it is used with MongoDB.

details.label: Practice
items: Connect your own development project to a MongoDB database.
Identify the database, collection and document in your Notes API.

tasks.title: Day 4: Finish the Notes database work · 01:20:00–01:43:39

details.label: Topics
items: Continue the Notes API database implementation.
Project overview.

details.label: Supplement to reach 30–50 min (10–20 min)
items: Mongoose CRUD methods: create, find, findById, findByIdAndUpdate, findByIdAndDelete.
Schema validation and MongoDB ObjectId basics.

details.label: Practice
items: Implement create, read, update and delete for notes.
Test successful requests and invalid IDs.

phases.name: Part A · Days 5–9: Backend project + frontend
phases.goal: Learn project structure, secrets and frontend-backend integration.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 9: connect a frontend to your backend and explain the request/response flow
phases.tip: Do not copy the project blindly; explain what each part does.

tasks.title: Day 5: Project architecture and backend setup · 01:43:39–02:20:00

details.label: Topics
items: Project overview and requirements.
Backend project structure and initial implementation.

details.label: Practice
items: Recreate the folder structure yourself.
Identify the purpose of each file and the flow from route to database.
Do not copy the project blindly; explain what each part does.

details.label: Topics
items: Continue backend development.
Connect the backend logic with the database and project requirements.

details.label: Practice
items: Rebuild the day's feature without looking at the video.
Test the relevant API endpoints in Postman.
Note any logic you cannot yet explain.

tasks.title: Day 7: Cloud setup and frontend introduction · 03:01:50–03:30:00

details.label: Topics
items: Cloud service setup and backend configuration.
Frontend project introduction.

details.label: Supplement to reach 30–50 min (5–15 min)
items: Environment variables and .env.
Why secrets and database credentials must not be committed to Git.
Difference between development and production configuration.

details.label: Practice
items: Create a local .env file and load configuration safely.
Add .env to .gitignore.

details.label: Topics
items: Frontend structure and application flow.
Understand which screens/features call which backend endpoints.

details.label: Practice
items: Trace one user action from the frontend to the API.
Write down the request method, URL, body and expected response.

details.label: Topics
items: Frontend-backend integration.
Authentication introduction and basic concepts.

details.label: Supplement if needed (5–15 min)
items: CORS and why browsers enforce it.
Same-origin policy and preflight requests.
API base URLs and handling failed HTTP responses.

details.label: Practice
items: Connect a frontend screen to your own API.
Test success, loading and error states.

phases.name: Part A · Days 10–13: Authentication + Spotify project
phases.goal: Understand token-based auth, JWT and cookies, then apply them in a project.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 11: explain and implement a basic registration/login flow
phases.tip: Never put passwords, secrets or sensitive personal data in a JWT payload.

details.label: Topics
items: Token-based authentication concepts.
Authentication implementation in code.

details.label: Practice
items: Draw the registration/login request flow.
Explain authentication vs authorization.
Identify where the password is hashed and where the token is created/verified.

details.label: Topics
items: JWT authentication.
Cookies, registration API and why tokens are used.

details.label: Practice
items: Implement or reproduce the registration/login flow.
Inspect a JWT's header, payload and signature using a safe local test.
Never put passwords, secrets or sensitive personal data in a JWT payload.

details.label: Topics
items: Spotify project overview.
Backend-focused project implementation.

details.label: Practice
items: Map the project's routes, controllers, models and database collections.
Rebuild one feature independently.

details.label: Topics
items: Continue the Spotify backend implementation.
Understand how the project's backend features fit together.

details.label: Practice
items: Test the implemented endpoints.
Explain the data flow from request to response.
List any unclear parts for revision.

phases.name: Part A · Days 14–15: Middleware, testing, validation
phases.goal: Learn middleware, then test and validate your API.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 15: add input validation and write basic API tests
phases.tip: Day 15's video end is not marked. If it runs past 50 min, split it with the +1 day button.

details.label: Topics
items: Middleware in Express.js.
Middleware chaining and request processing.

details.label: Practice
items: Write a simple logging middleware.
Write a middleware that checks whether a required header exists.
Understand req, res and next().

details.label: Video
details.text: 08:03:44–end of video

details.label: Topics
items: Jest and Supertest.
Express Validator and API validation.

details.label: Supplement
items: Unit tests vs integration tests.
Assertions and test cases.
Testing successful and failed API requests.
Validating untrusted user input.
details.text: Use the remaining lesson time, if needed, to understand:

details.label: Practice

Test missing, invalid and valid input.

details.label: Note
details.text: The supplied chapter list does not include the exact video end timestamp. Watch from 08:03:44 to the end, keeping the total lesson session within 30–50 minutes. If the remaining video itself exceeds 50 minutes, split it across two days.

phases.name: Part B · Days 16–20: Async, files, errors, data
phases.goal: Strengthen gaps a single crash course cannot cover in depth.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 20: model related MongoDB data and query it
phases.tip: Keep lessons to 30–50 min, then practise separately.

tasks.title: Day 16: Asynchronous JavaScript and the Node.js event loop

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Callbacks, Promises and async/await revision.
Event loop, call stack, microtasks and non-blocking I/O.

details.label: Why it matters
details.text: Database calls, file operations and network requests are asynchronous in Node.js.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Predict the output order of short examples using synchronous code, Promises and setTimeout.

tasks.title: Day 17: Node.js modules, files and streams

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: CommonJS vs ES Modules.
fs and path modules.
Buffers and streams: what they are and when to use them.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Read and write a local file using fs; compare reading a whole file with using a stream.

tasks.title: Day 18: Express error handling and application structure

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Centralized error-handling middleware.
next(error), HTTP error responses and avoiding duplicated try/catch logic.
Routes, controllers and services: separation of responsibilities.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Refactor one API route into route, controller and service files.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Filtering, sorting, projection and pagination.
Aggregation pipeline basics.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Add search, sorting and pagination to the Notes API.

tasks.title: Day 20: MongoDB data modelling and indexes

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Embedding vs referencing documents.
One-to-one and one-to-many relationships.
Indexes and why they improve query performance.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Model users and notes; decide which data should be referenced and add an index to a commonly queried field.

phases.name: Part B · Days 21–22: Auth and API security
phases.goal: Go beyond the tutorial on tokens, cookies and common attacks.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 22: apply essential API security protections
phases.tip: Implement only after understanding the security trade-offs.

tasks.title: Day 21: Authentication security beyond the tutorial

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Access tokens vs refresh tokens.
Token expiry, refresh and rotation.
HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite cookie settings.
Logout and token invalidation approaches.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Draw the login, authenticated request, refresh and logout flows. Implement only after understanding the security trade-offs.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Rate limiting and brute-force protection.
NoSQL injection and safe query construction.
CORS configuration.
XSS and CSRF: what they are and how they differ.
Input validation and sanitization.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Add validation and rate limiting to an authentication endpoint in a test project.

phases.name: Part B · Days 23–25: SQL, PostgreSQL, deployment
phases.goal: Learn relational basics, then deploy with production configuration.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 25: deploy an API with production configuration
phases.tip: Deploy a small API and verify its endpoints from Postman.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Tables, rows, columns and data types.
Primary keys and foreign keys.
SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Write basic SQL queries for users and projects.

tasks.title: Day 24: PostgreSQL and relational database design

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: PostgreSQL setup and connection.
Relationships and normalization basics.
Transactions and constraints.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Design users, projects and tasks tables with primary and foreign keys.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Deploying a Node.js/Express API.
Production environment variables.
Logs, graceful shutdown and basic monitoring.
Difference between local and production configuration.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Deploy a small API and verify its endpoints from Postman.

phases.name: Part B · Days 26–28: Docker, Redis, CI/CD
phases.goal: Understand common production tools and workflows.
phases.deliverable: Checkpoint Day 28: understand the purpose of common production tools and workflows
phases.tip: Treat these as introductions, not mastery.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: Docker images, containers and a basic Dockerfile.
Docker Compose fundamentals.
Swagger/OpenAPI: documenting endpoints.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Containerize a simple API or document its endpoints with an OpenAPI specification.

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: What caching is and why it is used.
Redis key-value model.
TTL and cache invalidation basics.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Sketch a cache-aside flow for a frequently requested API resource.

tasks.title: Day 28: CI/CD and system design introduction

details.label: Learn (30–50 min)
items: GitHub Actions fundamentals.
Automated test workflow.
Load balancing, horizontal scaling and caching concepts.

details.label: Practice
details.text: Create a simple workflow that runs tests on a push. Draw a basic scalable web application architecture.

notes.title: Daily time
notes.text: Lesson 30–50 min. Rebuild 60–90. Exercises 30–45. Debug 30–45. Notes 15–30. About 3–4 hours.

notes.title: Lesson cap
notes.text: Do not watch past the day's range. Finished early? Review that topic or read its docs. Do not start the next day.

notes.title: Need more time?
notes.text: Split the topic over another day. Do not rush.

notes.title: Checkpoints
notes.text: Do not move on because a video ended. Move on when you can do the task independently.

notes.title: Resources
notes.text: Extra links are references for specific gaps, not another full course.

notes.title: Timestamps
notes.text: Based on the chapter list supplied by you. Segment boundaries and supplement times are approximate.

notes.title: DSA: yes, lightly
notes.text: Helps fresher screening. JavaScript, 45–60 min/day, easy to medium.

notes.title: Next.js rule
notes.text: Finish Phase 0 first. What is left is parked, not failed.

notes.title: Git habit
notes.text: Commit daily. Your GitHub graph is part of the resume.

notes.title: Sunday review
notes.text: Tick progress. List 3 things you did not get. Fix those first.

notes.title: Buffer
notes.text: Sunday evening is free. Catch up, do not start new topics.
